threads.body: In declarative config mode (EarlyConfig.isDeclarativeConfig), boolean properties are translated to the `otel.instrumentation/development.java.*` namespace via evaluateBooleanProperty(), but the renamed logging key string properties are read directly without any translation. As a result, setting these keys via declarative-config-style property names won’t be picked up during ApplicationEnvironmentPreparedEvent, even though this class otherwise supports declarative config.

threads.body: `CommonConfig` logs a deprecation warning every time it is constructed with a deprecated declarative logging key present (e.g., `trace_id`). Since `CommonConfig` is instantiated from multiple builder utilities, this can lead to repeated warnings and log noise. Consider deduplicating these warnings (e.g., using a static `warnedDeprecatedProperties` set like `DbConfig` does in the same package).

threads.body: `ContextDataKeys` renamed `getTraceFlags()` to `getTraceFlagsKey()`, but there are still in-repo callers using the old getter (e.g., `instrumentation/log4j/log4j-appender-2.17/.../OpenTelemetryAppender` calls `contextDataKeys.getTraceFlags()`). Since this class is shared across modules, removing the old getter breaks those consumers. Consider keeping `getTraceFlags()` as a deprecated alias that returns `traceFlagsKey` (until all callers are migrated).

`ContextDataKeys.create(...)` is called on the hot path (e.g., once per log event in the Log4j appender). If a deprecated logging key setting is used, the current implementation will emit a deprecation warning every time `getConfig(...)` runs, which can flood logs. Consider tracking which deprecated properties have already been warned and only logging once per property.

threads.body: [Maintainability] Adding a class-level SLF4J logger named `logger` now shadows multiple existing local variables also named `logger` (of type `ch.qos.logback.classic.Logger`) in this class. This makes it harder to tell which logger is being referenced in different methods and increases the chance of mistakes during future edits. Consider renaming the SLF4J field (e.g., to `log`) to avoid the name collision.

threads.body: [Performance] `ContextDataKeys.create(...)` is invoked on the Log4j appender emit path (see `OpenTelemetryAppender.emit(...)`), and `getConfig(...)` may do multiple `ConfigPropertiesUtil.getString(...)` lookups when declarative config keys are not set. Because this can run per log event, repeated property lookups add overhead. Consider caching the resolved `ContextDataKeys` (e.g., once per `OpenTelemetry`/appender instance) so the system-property/declarative lookups and deprecated-name fallbacks are not performed on every log emission.
